passage:
Hey Afreen,
You asked what's new at school. Honestly, the best thing is our meme page. Me and Rustom made an account called "Pritam Daily" and we post edited pictures of him, his face on a crying baby, stuff like that. 200 followers already!
We also made a new chat for the class trip and just didn't add him. He'll figure it out.
It's weird. When I'm typing it, it feels like nothing. Just jokes on a screen. I never have to see his face when he reads them. Yesterday in the corridor he looked at me and I kind of looked away fast. Anyway.
How's college? Write back.
Zubin

qa.q: How many followers does the meme page have?
Why did Zubin look away fast in the corridor?
qa.a: Seeing Pritam's face in person made the jokes feel less like nothing, and Zubin probably felt a flicker of guilt.

qa.q: What could turn this around at this stage?
qa.a: Zubin could take the account down and add Pritam back, and Afreen could tell Zubin plainly that this is bullying and encourage a change to make it right.

qa.q: How does the meme page probably feel for Pritam?
qa.a: To Pritam it is heavy and public, with 200 people seeing edited pictures of him, while for Zubin it is only typing.

grounding: It shows mocking moving to edited photos, a fake account and exclusion from plans, feeling light to the sender behind a screen but heavy for the target.

passage:
Bidisha, you want to know about Tulika? Fine. I'm Nazia, and I'm not proud of this. Last year it started as jokes at lunch. Then it went online. Someone made a fake profile with her name and posted silly things as if she wrote them. We made a trip plan chat and just left her out. I sent the edited photo to three groups. I sent it from my bed, eating chips, laughing. It felt like nothing. Honestly, it felt like a game.
Then one day I passed her near the bus stop. She was holding her phone, and her eyes were swollen. She didn't even look angry, just empty. That's when it hit me. On my side it was one tap. On her side it was all day, every day.

qa.a: Nazia passed her near the bus stop.

qa.q: What did Nazia realise on seeing Tulika's face?
qa.a: Nazia realised that what felt light while lying in bed was heavy for Tulika all day, and Nazia seems to feel guilty.

qa.q: What could Nazia do now to start repairing the harm?
qa.a: Nazia could stop sharing, report the fake profile, apologise to Tulika and tell a trusted adult what happened so it can be dealt with.

qa.q: How might Bidisha react to hearing this?
qa.a: Bidisha might be shocked but also see that Nazia is being honest, and could encourage Nazia to act on that feeling.

grounding: It illustrates bullying escalating to a fake profile, edited photos and exclusion, with the screen making it feel light to the sender and heavy to the target.
